catalyst.notes: All 3 ML sources agree on Pd/XPhos, while SCDB suggests Pd(PPh3)4

solvent.notes: ML suggests cyclopentyl methyl ether, 1,4-dioxane, or 2-methyl-2-butanol; SCDB suggests 1,4-dioxane

temperature.notes: Only SCDB provides temperature (60°C), ML sources lack temperature data

base.notes: ML suggests t-BuOK, t-BuONa, or KOH; SCDB suggests K2CO3

synthesis.confidence_reasoning: Medium confidence due to partial catalyst agreement (3/4 sources suggest Pd catalysis) but significant solvent/base divergence. ML confidence scores are very low (0.01), indicating poor similarity to training data.

recommended_condition.rationale: Selected Pd/XPhos based on ML consensus for this Buchwald-Hartwig amination of bromobenzene with aniline. 1,4-dioxane chosen as common solvent across ML and SCDB sources. Elevated temperature (80°C) recommended over SCDB's 60°C to ensure complete conversion. K3PO4 selected as robust base for aryl bromides with anilines.

backup_conditions.when_to_use: <30% conv: SPhos offers similar electron-rich properties with potentially better performance for aryl bromides
<20% after 12h: Traditional Pd/PPh3 system as reliable fallback

warnings: Monitor for proto-debromination side reaction with strong bases
Ensure anhydrous conditions for Pd catalysis
Aniline may require purification to remove moisture
Consider molecular sieves if water-sensitive conditions needed

source_comparison.ml_contribution: Provided catalyst/ligand consensus (Pd/XPhos) but with low confidence scores
source_comparison.rule_contribution: Provided solvent (1,4-dioxane) and temperature guidance from SCDB database
